headline: Two days to the start line, and the taper has done its job cleanly. Legs fresh, engine banked, strength held live to the edge. From here the trail writes it.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The picture is exactly what a well-executed pre-event quiet should look like: running has dropped to short, low-HR shakeouts sitting almost entirely in the easy zones, while the four-week block still carries a meaningful volume bump over the prior four weeks — you arrive with recent load banked, not bled off. Strength stayed frequent right into the final week, which matters more than usual here because a 6–8 kg pack over 580 km is a durability problem before it's an aerobic one. Steps remain high off the bike commute and daily movement, so the taper is a running taper, not a movement shutdown. The "detraining" cardio-load status is a rolling-average artefact of deliberately suppressed recent running load, not a real signal — read it as evidence the taper landed, nothing more.
sections.trends: The year-to-date gap over last year is enormous, and the 16-week shape shows a genuine build peaking with the long efforts in late July before this intentional drawdown. That arc — accumulate, sharpen, quiet — is coherent for someone standing on the edge of a multi-day crossing rather than a sign of a plateau. The four-week increase over the prior block confirms the build was real and recent; the current dip is the narrowest, most deliberate part of the curve, not a reversal of it.
sections.threshold: Threshold pace and its anchoring HR have held flat across the 30-day window, which in taper context is the outcome you want — sharpening should preserve the engine, not chip at it. Nothing in the recent easy runs contradicts that: the aerobic system is intact and steady. For the crossing itself, threshold speed is largely irrelevant; what it tells you now is simply that the base you built didn't erode while you rested it.
sections.zones: The recent sessions are almost purely Z1/Z2, which is precisely correct this close to a long self-supported effort — there's no reason to touch Z4/Z5 with the start line this near. The one genuinely hard session in the window was the long late-July run, which carried real Z3/Z4 time and served its purpose before the quiet began. Since then the distribution has narrowed exactly as a taper should: no grey-zone drift, no accidental intensity creeping into what are meant to be shakeouts.
sections.hr_comparison: The strength sessions have run without chest-strap data recently, so there's nothing new to read there this week; the earlier strength HR entries sat sensibly low, consistent with functional work rather than a second conditioning session. On the runs, avg-to-max spreads look clean and orderly, with the recent easy efforts sitting comfortably below where the same paces cost you under fatigue — no source-agreement concerns worth flagging.
sections.calendar: The running streak sits at its all-time best and the strength streak is holding, which is the more important story than any single week's volume. The consistency going into this crossing is the asset — you're not arriving off a fragmented block, you're arriving off the most sustained stretch you've logged. That's the durability foundation the next ten days will draw on.
sections.personal_bests: None of the speed PBs are relevant to this window — they belong to a sharpening phase, not a taper before a multi-day trek. The one worth keeping in mind is the 50K/136 km mark from the long attempt; the crossing is a different beast (staged, packed, hilly), but it sits in the same durability territory, and how the back-to-back days hold will tell you more about that capacity than any timed effort could.

watch_items: Watch how "easy" HR recalibrates once loaded days start stacking under the pack — the first two or three days will reset your sense of what steady costs.
Track the back-to-back leg response early; cumulative durability under load, not the engine, remains the real unknown.
Read the border mountain crossing as its own terrain spike, distinct from the flatter coastal running.
Watch whether nightly recovery settles once trail rhythm replaces the travel-and-logistics window.
